title: Gannibal
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Police officer Daigo Agawa transfers with his family to the remote mountain village of Kuge after his predecessor vanishes. When an old woman's body is found with a human bite mark, the villagers, led by the powerful Goto family, turn hostile, and Daigo begins to suspect rumors that the village eats people.
life_message: Truth and the protection of one's family are worth pursuing even against a closed community's dark secrets.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Goto clan loyalty and Daigo's family protection drive conflict; story critiques clan closure.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Village ritual versus modern law; story sides with law.

folkways.japan: The closed rural village (mura shakai) wary of outsiders is a common setting in Japanese horror and reflects real tensions between rural communities and newcomers.

delivery.evidence: ANN praises layered thematic threads; no reviewer calls it preachy (to verify).
delivery.note: Summaries describe a mystery that reveals its themes through investigation rather than speeches.

winners_losers: Daigo and the law get sympathy; the Goto clan's secrecy is the threat, though the ANN review notes the cannibalism is first framed as a post-death ritual rather than simple malice.
